source_documents.title: Photophysical behavior of mono- and bis(2′-hydroxyphenyl)-6-(4′-diphenylaminophenyl)pyrimidines: Interplay of ESIPT, ICT, and vibrational nonradiative decay

reference_evidence_units.quote: all compounds exhibit very low fluores cence quantum yields
reference_evidence_units.subject: compounds 1-4
reference_evidence_units.statement: Very weak fluorescence under neutral conditions.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Although ESIPT is energetically accessible according to TD-DFT calculations, the absence of a significant decrease in oscillator strength upon enol–keto conversion suggests that ESIPT alone does not fully account for the observed quenching.
reference_evidence_units.subject: compounds 1-4
reference_evidence_units.statement: ESIPT is accessible but not the main quenching channel.

reference_evidence_units.quote: indicating that large-amplitude molecular motions, particularly involving the diphenylamino group, play a major role in promoting in ternal conversion
reference_evidence_units.subject: compounds 1-4
reference_evidence_units.statement: Low-frequency motions of the diphenylamino group drive internal conversion.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Protonation of the pyrimidine nitrogen atoms induces pronounced bathochromic shifts in both absorption and emission spectra, reflecting an enhancement of the ICT character.
reference_evidence_units.subject: compounds 1-4

reference_mechanisms.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Quenching is attributed to coupling with large-amplitude motions of the diphenylamino group. Boundary case (RIM vs RADIATIVE): quenching through an intramolecular motion whose barrier or coupling is tuned by substituents, not restricted by an environment; labelled RIM by guideline §3.2 (access to a conical intersection along a motion).

reference_mechanisms.label: ESIPT_PT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: ESIPT is accessible but judged not to account for the quenching.
